newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo bolsa volume soars on Telebras trade.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo bolsa volume soars on Telebras trade.

text.p: Trading volume on the Sao Paulo bourse surged to 1.08 billion reais ($1 billion) by mid-afternoon on block trades and speculation on benchmark Telebras, brokers said.
"There's cross trades and block trades and even derivatives trade boosting volume," a local dealer told Reuters.
Brokers also said intense speculation on Telebras, which accounted for 600 million reais or 66.3 percent of total trade, drove up the market.
Telebras' preferred was up a strong 1.6 percent at 159 reais to lead the 0.75 percent rise in the Bovespa index to 12,298 points at 1505 local time/1405 EDT.
Telebras common was up 2.28 percent at 143.70 reais.

Wednesday's lower house approval of a new General Telecommunications Law may have sparked Telebras' rise, but traders said the stock has already factored in that news, prompting talk of a correction before the session's end.
Indeed, the preferred was off today's high of 160.50 reais.
Dealers also reported heavy trade in blue chip Petrobras Both stocks fell, with Petrobras off 3.56 percent at 298 reais, and Eletrobras was down 0.96 percent at 617 reais.
Around 15.4 million reais of Eletrobras preferred B traded, while Petrobras preferred volume was 31.2 million reais.
"There's really no news, nothing to justify the rise, so it's just speculation," one trader said, adding some investors may have been anticipating Friday's Telebras options expirations in New York.
Derivatives accounted for 300 million reais worth of volume by mid-afternoon, but the more than 700 million reais in stock transactions almost two hours before the close was still high.
Daily average trade has been steadily rising in recent weeks and volume surged both Monday and Wednesday due to expiration of options and futures respectively.
But brokers said Thursday's heavy trade may signal a change in trading patterns after the market's bull run on swollen volume over the past several weeks.
"Usually, when you have such heavy volume for no reason on a regular day like today it means there may be a change in trading patterns," a dealer said.
